classification.difficultyReason: Connects a scaled tangent substitution, quartic roots, factorisation and selection of an exact trigonometric value.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the identity $\tan4\theta=\dfrac{4\tan\theta-4\tan^3\theta}{1-6\tan^2\theta+\tan^4\theta}$ to find the values of $\theta$ such that $x=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\tan\theta$ is a solution of $P(x)=0$.

answer.short:
$\theta=\dfrac\pi{12}+\dfrac{k\pi}{4}$, $k\in\mathbb Z$.

Four representatives modulo $\pi$ are $\dfrac\pi{12},\dfrac\pi3,\dfrac{7\pi}{12},\dfrac{5\pi}6$. The substitution reduces the equation to $\tan4\theta=\sqrt3$.
answer.worked:
Let $t=\tan\theta$, so $x=\frac{t}{\sqrt3}$.
$$\begin{align*}P(t/\sqrt3)&=t^4+\frac4{\sqrt3}t^3-6t^2-\frac4{\sqrt3}t+1\\P(t/\sqrt3)&=(1-6t^2+t^4)-\frac1{\sqrt3}(4t-4t^3).\end{align*}$$
Thus $P(x)=0$ gives
$$\begin{align*}1-6t^2+t^4&=\frac1{\sqrt3}(4t-4t^3)\\\frac{4t-4t^3}{1-6t^2+t^4}&=\sqrt3\\\tan4\theta&=\sqrt3\\4\theta&=\frac\pi3+k\pi\\\theta&=\frac\pi{12}+\frac{k\pi}{4},\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.\end{align*}$$
The denominator cannot be zero at a solution: a zero denominator would require $4t-4t^3=0$, but $t=0,\pm1$ do not make the denominator zero. Four representatives modulo $\pi$ are $\frac{\pi}{12},\frac{\pi}{3},\frac{7\pi}{12},\frac{5\pi}{6}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Explain why $(x-1)(3x+1)$ is a factor of $P(x)$.

answer.short: $\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$ and $\frac{5\pi}{6}$ give $x=1$ and $-\frac{1}{3}$. By the factor theorem, $(x-1)(3x+1)$ is a factor.
answer.worked:
$\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$ and $\frac{5\pi}{6}$ are solutions from part (a).
$$\begin{align*}\frac1{\sqrt3}\tan\frac\pi3&=1\\\frac1{\sqrt3}\tan\frac{5\pi}6&=-\frac13.\end{align*}$$
Hence $P(1)=P(-\frac{1}{3})=0$. By the factor theorem, $x-1$ and $x+\frac{1}{3}$ are distinct factors, so their product, equivalently $(x-1)(3x+1)$, is a factor of $P(x)$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: By finding the other zeroes of $P(x)$ in surd form, find the exact value of $\tan\left(\dfrac\pi{12}\right)$, giving reasons.

answer.short:
Other zeroes: $-1\pm\dfrac{2\sqrt3}{3}$.

$\tan(\frac{\pi}{12})=2-\sqrt3$. Divide out the known factors, then select the positive tangent value.
answer.worked:
Dividing out the factors from part (b),
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(3x+1)(3x^2+6x-1)\\3x^2+6x-1&=0\\x&=\frac{-6\pm\sqrt{36+12}}6\\x&=-1\pm\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}.\end{align*}$$
The other tangent values are therefore
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\sqrt3x\\\tan\theta&=-\sqrt3\pm2.\end{align*}$$
The known roots $1$ and $-\frac{1}{3}$ correspond to $\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$ and $\frac{5\pi}{6}$ modulo $\pi$. Thus $\frac{\pi}{12}$ corresponds to one of the other roots. Since $0<\frac{\pi}{12}<\frac{\pi}{2}$, its tangent is positive:
$$\tan\frac\pi{12}=2-\sqrt3.$$
